drivingQuestion: Whom did the chandelier's signal serve?

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע שַׁחֲרִית עִם אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר, וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲמָד — לֹא יָצָא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מַשְׁכִּימִין וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲמָד מֵאֲחֵרִים! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לִשְׁאָר עַמָּא דְּבִירוּשְׁלֶם.
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection: One who recites Shema» in the «morning with the men of the priestly watch,» who served in the Temple during a given week, «or with the men of the non-priestly watch,» designated groups of Israelites who accompanied the priestly watch to Jerusalem that week, «did not fulfill» his obligation. That is «because the men of the priestly watch» recite Shema too «early» so that they will have sufficient time to perform the Temple service, «and the men of the non-priestly watch,» who recite lengthy prayers and stand over the daily morning offering when it is sacrificed, «postpone» reciting Shema. For whom, then, did the emanating sparks signal the time to recite Shema? «Abaye said:» It was an indicator «for the rest of the people in Jerusalem,» who recited Shema at the appropriate time to recite Shema.

moves.summary: the Temple watches do not recite at sunrise

moves.about: the signal served the rest of Jerusalem's people

edges.about: neither the priestly watch nor the non-priestly watch recite Shema at sunrise, so whom did the chandelier signal?
the signal served the rest of Jerusalem's people

positions.claim: it signaled the rest of Jerusalem's residents
